standard_prerequisites.name: Fiber of a pointed map
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fiber of f : X -> Y at y_0 is Sigma x:X (f x = y_0), pointed at (x_0, f_0).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose iterated fibers the statement describes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Iterated maps f^(n) of the fiber sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The maps f^(n) are the successive projections and connecting maps of the fiber sequence, with f^(n-1) o f^(n) = 0.
standard_prerequisites.use: The three parts of the statement are about f^(1), f^(2) and f^(3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Associativity of sigma types
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sigma types reassociate up to equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the first step of the displayed chain at source line 1014.

core_obligations: For part (1), unpack the fiber of f^(1) = proj1 as a triple (x, p, q) and reassociate by the sigma associativity result (source lines 1010-1014).
Contract the sigma type of x together with x = x_0, rewrite the remaining type as f(x_0) = y_0 and then as y_0 = y_0, which is definitionally Omega Y (source lines 1015-1017).

Trace the equivalence explicitly, showing that it sends ((x,p),q) to opp(f_0) `ct` ap f (opp q) `ct` p, and check that the basepoint is sent to the basepoint so that the map is pointed (source lines 1018-1021).
Identify f^(2) with the map r |-> (x_0, f_0 `ct` r) under this equivalence (source line 1022).
Obtain part (2) by applying part (1) to f^(1) in place of f, and read off the identification of f^(3) with Omega f composed with reversal (source lines 1024-1028).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack the fiber and reassociate the sigma types.
Contract and reduce to Omega Y.
Compute the equivalence explicitly and check it is pointed; identify f^(2).
Iterate for part (2) and identify f^(3).

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 8.4.4 at source lines 1001-1008, in three parts: the fiber of the first map of the fiber sequence is Omega Y, the fiber of the second is Omega X, and under these equivalences the third map is identified with Omega f composed with path reversal. The author's proof (source lines 1009-1028) is a computation rather than a citation: it unpacks the fiber as a triple and reassociates the sigma types (lines 1011-1014), contracts one component to reduce the type to y_0 = y_0 (lines 1015-1017), and then works out the resulting equivalence explicitly, checking both that it sends ((x,p),q) to opp(f_0) `ct` ap f (opp q) `ct` p and that it preserves basepoints so that it is a map of pointed types (lines 1018-1021). Part (2) is an iteration, and part (3) requires following f^(3) through the identification of f^(2) (lines 1022-1028). The statement gives the three equivalences without any of the explicit formulas.
